comments.body:
Let's keep original code on launch normal in case it is !firstEnableCall
I do have reason on it and you will see later on.
The major purpose is keep logic for "Retry" only a special case for firstTimeRetry,
We should check if it is still "enable", as well as "launched successfully once" in the past here before call launchApp.

I will suggest to move this one to LaunchApp method.
As the result, if there is other calling LaunchApp other than this "First time RetryMethod", then we can stop.

Given, it is just a bool, we don't have problem on concurrent read here.
For concurrent write, we also don't have, thus I think we don't need to make it as atomic here.

instead, they can be just like the firstEnableCall
Let's name this as "FirstTimeRetryLaunch", we can get rid of the bool here.
I don't think raw bool will make sure thread visibility on change, but atomic<bool> will
What do you mean? This method should be called in only if it's by enable(). And first time attempt is safe. The second time will check enable in line 311
I mean they are for different purpose with different logic unit.  Why we should mix them into one?

line 311 is not right after the std::this_thread::sleep_for.
NOTE: line 311 make senses now.

And here, right after "std::this_thread::sleep_for", we should check again, since the world can be changed already.
Make sense, check should be right after sleep.

Retry covers logic for retry or not retry. That function covers logic for handling whether retry and retry count management. 
We need to check whether retry, and I put logic inside retry, this keeps code here clean to me
